questions.prompt: What burden does MCP shift away from your application?

choices.B: Writing and maintaining tool definitions and their execution for outside services

questions.explanation: MCP servers expose ready-made tools, prompts and resources.

questions.prompt: "Isn't MCP just tool use?" What is the right answer?

choices.B: No: tool use is how Claude calls tools; MCP is about who provides and runs them (a server someone built)

questions.explanation: They're complementary.

questions.prompt: Who can author an MCP server?

choices.B: Anyone; service providers often publish official ones

questions.explanation: e.g. an official AWS or GitHub server.

questions.prompt: What three kinds of things can an MCP server expose?
questions.explanation: The three server primitives.

questions.prompt: What does "transport-agnostic" mean for MCP?

choices.B: Client and server can talk over stdio, HTTP, WebSockets or other transports

questions.explanation: stdio on the same machine is most common.

questions.prompt: Which message pair discovers available tools?
questions.explanation: CallTool runs one.

questions.prompt: In the full flow, who decides to call a tool?

choices.B: Claude, after receiving the tool list with the question

questions.explanation: Your server then asks the client to run it.

questions.prompt: Who actually calls the GitHub API in the course's example flow?
questions.explanation: The server wraps the outside service.

questions.prompt: How do you create a server with the Python SDK?
questions.explanation: One line with FastMCP.

questions.prompt: How are tool argument schemas produced with the SDK?

choices.B: Generated from type hints and Pydantic Field descriptions

questions.explanation: Decorators plus type hints do the work.

questions.prompt: read_doc_contents receives an unknown doc_id. What does the course do?

choices.B: Raise a ValueError with a clear message

questions.explanation: Errors surface to the client and model.

questions.prompt: Which decorator registers a tool?
questions.explanation: Resources and prompts have their own decorators.

questions.prompt: How do you start the MCP Inspector for your server?
questions.explanation: Then open the local URL it prints.

questions.prompt: What is the first thing to click in the Inspector?
questions.explanation: Connect starts the server; then list tools.

questions.prompt: You edit a document with a tool, then read it in the Inspector. Why does the change show?

choices.C: It rewrites the file on disk

questions.explanation: Useful for testing multi-step interactions.

questions.prompt: Why use the Inspector?

choices.B: To test and debug tools quickly without wiring up the full app

questions.explanation: Fast feedback loop.

questions.prompt: Why wrap ClientSession in your own MCPClient class?

choices.B: The session needs careful resource cleanup; the wrapper manages it

questions.explanation: Your class handles connection lifecycle.

questions.prompt: What does list_tools() return in the course client?
questions.explanation: Those tools are sent to Claude.

questions.prompt: Where do the tool name and input for call_tool come from?
questions.explanation: The app forwards Claude's request to the server.

questions.prompt: How do you quickly test the client alone?
questions.explanation: Then run main.py for the full flow.

questions.prompt: What are MCP resources for?

choices.B: Exposing data to read, similar to GET handlers

questions.explanation: Tools act; resources provide data.

questions.prompt: Which is a templated resource?
questions.explanation: Parameters in the URI become function arguments.

questions.prompt: What does mime_type on a resource do?

choices.B: Hints to clients how to interpret the returned data

questions.explanation: e.g. application/json vs text/plain.

questions.prompt: Where do templated resources appear in the Inspector?
questions.explanation: Direct ones are under Resources.

questions.prompt: How does the client read a resource?
questions.explanation: Then parse according to the MIME type.

questions.prompt: The resource MIME type is application/json. What does the client do?

choices.B: json.loads the text and return the object

questions.explanation: Other types return the text as is.

questions.prompt: Why is inserting a mentioned document via a resource nicer than a tool call?

choices.B: The content goes straight into the prompt, so Claude answers without an extra tool round trip

questions.explanation: App-controlled context injection.

questions.prompt: In the CLI, what triggers resource autocomplete?
questions.explanation: / is for prompts.

questions.prompt: Why would a server author ship prompts?

choices.B: To give users well-crafted, tested instructions that beat ad-hoc wording

questions.explanation: Encoded expertise, consistency, reuse.

questions.prompt: What does an @mcp.prompt function return?
questions.explanation: Can include user and assistant messages.

questions.prompt: How are prompt arguments like doc_id used?
questions.explanation: Check the rendered messages in the Inspector.

questions.prompt: Which is a stated benefit of server prompts?

choices.B: Update in one place to improve all clients

questions.explanation: Also consistency and encoded expertise.

questions.prompt: How does the client fetch a prompt with its arguments?
questions.explanation: args become the prompt function's keyword arguments.

questions.prompt: In the CLI, how does a user discover prompts?
questions.explanation: Prompts appear as slash commands.

questions.prompt: After fetching the "format" prompt, what happens?

choices.A: The server formats the document itself
choices.B: The messages go to Claude, which uses tools (read/edit) to do the work

questions.explanation: Prompts drive Claude; tools do the actions.

questions.prompt: The args dict for the format prompt would look like...
questions.explanation: A mapping of argument names to string values.

questions.prompt: Which primitive is model-controlled?
questions.explanation: Claude decides when to call tools.

questions.prompt: Which primitive is user-controlled?
questions.explanation: Users trigger them (buttons, slash commands).

questions.prompt: You want to populate an autocomplete list in your UI with data from the server. Which primitive?
questions.explanation: Resources are app-controlled data.

questions.prompt: Match each to a primitive: "Add from Google Drive", a "summarize" workflow button, Claude running code.
questions.answer: Google Drive import = resource (app-controlled); workflow button = prompt (user-controlled); running code = tool (model-controlled).
questions.explanation: Tools serve the model, resources the app, prompts the user.
